# 2.2: generated Go vs hand-written Go

Each fixture is a real aimux-core value serialized with serde (the truth). It is decoded and re-marshaled by the generated Go (`aimux-codegen --emit go`) and by the hand-written `bindings/go/types.go` + `multimodal_types.go` + the `RawToolCall` type and codec from `repair.go` (the rest of repair.go needs cgo). A row is a JSON path where the two outputs differ. The verdict says which side disagrees with the Rust output. The test also requires the generated output to equal the Rust output for every fixture.

## Rules

- Numbers are compared by numeric value only at JSON paths whose IR type is `f32` / `f64` (`float_paths` + `json_eq_at`, tools/aimux-codegen/tests/common/float_paths.rs:267): Go writes an `f64` zero as `0`, serde as `0.0`, the same JSON value. Every other number, integers included, must match exactly (2^53+1 ≠ 2^53). No other normalization is applied.
- A `TypeTag` type (`ToolCall`, `RawToolCall`, `Source`) is sampled where the FFI uses it standalone, with its `type` tag (`aimux_core::wire::Tagged` / `typed` / `typed_vec`: aimux-ffi/src/lib.rs:1972, aimux-core/src/parse_tool_call.rs:625, aimux-core/src/generate.rs:575-583), and compared with the generated `Tagged<T>`.
- Every `手写错` row below is a U1 finding about the hand-written Go. U1 does not modify the hand-written Go; it is removed in U3, when the generated code replaces it.
